## Known biases

Everything comes from what a vendor&\#x27;s operators could see in street-level photos and LiDAR from the road: buildings hidden by construction or obstruction (135,503 rows) have estimated grade, 14,039 rows have no measurement (value 0), and subgrade space reachable only from inside (cellars in large buildings) is not recorded, so &\#x27;no subgrade&\#x27; means &\#x27;none seen&\#x27;. Small accessory buildings such as sheds are excluded. The 1,000-row sample fetched is the first 1,000 by BIN and covers Manhattan only.

<details><summary>Passage: grade estimates</summary>

<pre>In many instances where the lowest adjacent grade was below street level, the derived measurement in the dataset is an estimate. Any building centroid that has an estimated grade elevation will note “Property not visible due to construction or obstruction” under note_1. Estimates were made by individual data operators based on context clues in the imagery.
[dictionary] While note_1 records if estimates were taken, there is no record of which of the two observed measurements (or both) was the estimated value. DCP has established that the accuracy of estimated spot elevations is reasonable provided that one of the methodologies previously described has been followed.
[dictionary, z_grade] When no measurement has been taken, the field value will be 0</pre>
